The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it encrypts your login. ImmichCtrl will sign out of every account and remove its offline albums, cached photos and backup history from this phone. Your photos on the Immich server and the photos on this phone stay.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to sign out and sign in again.
ImmichCtrl\'s app lock now has its own PIN, separate from your phone\'s. Your login is encrypted with it while the app is locked.
Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening ImmichCtrl. While locked, your login stays encrypted with the PIN, and the photo widgets hide your photos.

ImmichCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your own Immich server (and its map tiles when maps are on). While automatic backup (or admin alerts on an admin account) is on, that account\'s login stays usable in the background for backups and alerts. Every other login stays encrypted with the PIN while the app is locked.

Secure connection failed: %1$s. If your server only supports plain HTTP, type http:// in front of the address.

ImmichCtrl couldn\'t connect to this server over HTTPS. It can try plain HTTP instead, but then your password and photos are sent unencrypted and anyone on the network can see them. Only do this on a network you trust.

Removes photos and videos from this phone that are backed up to Immich and not in its trash. They stay on the server. Removed items go to the phone\'s trash first, so empty it there to get the space back. Photos other apps use (like WhatsApp chats) may look blurry or missing there afterwards; keep those albums below.
You can restore them from the trash in Library for %1$s days. Photos only on this phone go to the phone\'s trash.
You can restore them from the trash in Library for %1$s days.
The app always uses the address you pick here and never switches by itself. Pick the public address before you leave your home network.
Your server\'s address on your home network, e.g. its IP and port: faster, and it works even if the internet is down. Save it, then pick it under Address in use. Leave empty to remove it.

This address uses plain HTTP. While you use it, the app sends your sign-in and photos to it unencrypted, so anyone on that network can read them. The app doesn\'t check which network you\'re on: on another network, a different device could be at the same address. Only use it on a home network you trust, and pick the public address before you leave.

Your timeline, albums and partners\' photos are kept on this phone (only the list of photos, not the photos themselves) and only changes are downloaded, so Photos opens straight away. Nothing from the locked folder is kept. Reset sync deletes this copy and downloads it again.

The copy of your timeline on this phone is deleted and downloaded again from the server. Your photos aren\'t touched. Until it\'s done, Photos loads month by month.
